text:
jon: FYI reproducible perf regression on Dedicated: p95 token latency jumps ~2x when micro-batch fanout > 64. heap/profile attached: https://gist.github.com/foo/heap-2026-tiny-slab.txt :confused:
maria: can you paste the short allocator log around the spike? wondering if it's fragmentation or pinned memory saturation
jon: pasted minimal trace below. notice lot of tiny frees but no large coalesces: 
```
[2026-03-22T14:02:11Z] allocator: alloc size=24KB slab=tiny id=0x8f2a
[2026-03-22T14:02:11Z] allocator: alloc size=16KB slab=tiny id=0x8f2b
[2026-03-22T14:02:11Z] evictor: pin_success=0 pin_fail=7 reason=fragmentation
[2026-03-22T14:02:12Z] evictor: staging_used=976MB staging_limit=1024MB
[2026-03-22T14:02:12Z] allocator: alloc_failed size=128KB reason=no_contig_chunk
```

tara: sounds like tiny-slab fragmentation + host staging pressure. different angle than recent offload quota incidents: here tiny allocations accumulate and prevent reclaim of larger churned objects
lisa: two immediate questions: 1) can we treat tiny allocations as reclaimable first-class? 2) do we need per-tenant tiny-slab caps to avoid noisy neighbors?
omar: +1 on per-tenant tiny-slab. also propose a separate tiny-slab allocator that maintains 4KB subpages but groups them into compact superpages so we can reclaim large contiguous extents when needed
jon: design sketch: introduce tiny-slab namespace with parameters: {subpage=4KB, superpage=1MB, reclaimable=true, tenant_cap=~10%pool}. allocator alloc API becomes alloc(size, AllocHint) where AllocHint includes hotness_hint and offloadable=true/false. default offloadable=true for KV caches
maria: API change is fine, but we should minimize allocation hot paths touching metadata. propose compact 8-byte header per allocation: 1B class, 1B flags, 6B owner/id -> then allocator can answer "is_offloadable" cheaply without extra lookup
tara: tradeoffs: compact header increases per-alloc overhead vs current design where metadata is separate. but it avoids a hash/lookup on hot path. also matters for tiny allocations where header overhead is a big fraction
lisa: operational mitigations until RFC lands: 1) enable aggressive tiny-slab compaction sweep (increase sweep_rate by 3x) 2) cap tiny-slab growth per tenant to X MB 3) add metric tiny_alloc_density (tiny_allocs / total_allocs) and tiny_fragmentation_ratio (wasted_bytes / total_bytes)
omar: testing: add unit/integration test that simulates N tenants each doing M concurrent 8-32KB allocations and asserts that fallback to host-commit or offload occurs within 50ms and that staging_used doesn't exceed threshold
jon: rollout plan: emergency config change (sweep_rate/cap) -> canary on one Dedicated pool -> monitor tiny_fragmentation_ratio, staging_used, alloc_fail_rate_by_bin for 30m -> if stable, roll cluster-wide
maria: logging improvement: when allocation fails for "no_contig_chunk" include last_compaction_age and tiny_slab_free_runs to speed triage
ora: (typo in participants list earlier) — tagging ops: @devops-bot please create INC if we hit alloc_fail_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m
devops-bot: alert: creating INC-2026-415: tiny-slab fragmentation causing alloc_fail_rate spike
jon: long-term RFC items to capture: - tiny-slab design + superpage compaction algorithm - compact 8-byte allocation header format - per-tenant soft/hard tiny-slab caps + borrowing semantics - allocation hint semantics (atomic_reserve at request start) - telemetry contract (per-alloc lifetime histogram by size bin)
maria: also propose a background GC pass that coalesces free subpages into superpages, gated by tenant fairness so we don't starve live workloads
tara: performance note: compaction will add CPU overhead. we should simulate on perf rig to measure CPU vs latency tradeoff. include CPU per-request and wall-time compaction cost in RFC
lisa: please include explicit metrics to watch in RFC: staging_used, tiny_fragmentation_ratio, alloc_fail_rate_by_bin, compaction_cpu_ms, tiny_slab_used_by_tenant
jon: I'll draft RFC and emergency config PRs. tagging @maria @tara @omar for review. thanks all :thumbsup:
